## Prediction Markets Expand Beyond Retail


**Executive Summary:**


- Picture this: a stock reports earnings, beats on both EPS and revenue, yet falls on higher than expected capex guidance. Sound familiar? Many investors have been in this position when trading company earnings – they made the right fundamental call but still ended up with negative PnL because the stock price decoupled from the earnings metric. Until now, institutional investors had few tools to monetize their fundamental view of a stock without taking on the stock’s whole price reaction.
- **Cboe is launching KPI binary options on 23 of the most actively traded US companies to help address that gap** . KPI options allow investors to isolate fundamental risk from price risk, since a stock’s price reaction to earnings reflects not just the results, but also guidance, positioning, and the macro tape. KPI options also let investors express segment-level views (such as AWS or iPhone sales), trade market share dynamics between competitors (such as AMD vs NVDA data center revenue), hedge a specific layer of the AI trade, or build a basket of cyclical indicators to hedge economic downturn risk. Contract prices also tell you the market’s implied probability of a beat, making them a real-time complement to analyst consensus.
- The mechanics are simple: each KPI contract is a binary call or put option on a specific company metric, such as EPS, Revenue, or Operating Margin, that pays $1 if the reported number meets the stated condition at expiry and $0 if it does not. See chart below and full product[listing details here](https://go.cboe.com/e/77532/y-Options-Product-Listings-pdf/frvx89/1478547692/h/3QM9cnX21esOtO6MLoAaIbjOGdNUCfsproIZObVXd1c) . More information can also be found on the Cboe pre-launch[resource hub](https://go.cboe.com/e/77532/hought-leadership-resource-hub/frvx8d/1478547692/h/3QM9cnX21esOtO6MLoAaIbjOGdNUCfsproIZObVXd1c) .
- Although corporate event contracts are still a nascent part of the prediction market, they’re growing rapidly. At present, existing KPI contracts trade primarily on CFTC-regulated venues geared toward retail. Cboe’s KPI binary options take a different route: they are SEC-regulated securities options built on the listed-options framework that many institutions already know, which could make onboarding easier from a risk, compliance, and workflow perspective. Bringing institutional flow alongside the current retail trading could mean tighter spreads and deeper liquidity for everyone.[Read the full report](https://go.cboe.com/e/77532/ht-leadership-read-full-report/frvx8h/1478547692/h/3QM9cnX21esOtO6MLoAaIbjOGdNUCfsproIZObVXd1c) to see institutional use cases for KPI options.
